items.title: Payment requested for private land register entry
items.computation: The letter prints a fixed calendar date for payment: 01.12.2026. This date is taken as written; no period calculation is needed. 2026-12-01 is a Tuesday, not a weekend or public holiday in NW, so no shift applies. Note, however, that the letter itself states this document is only an offer ('Dieses Schreiben ist ein Angebot') and that a contract only comes into existence if and when payment is made ('ein Vertrag kommt erst durch die Zahlung zustande'). This means there is, as of now, no existing contractual obligation to pay anything by this or any date; the printed deadline is the sender's own commercial pressure date for accepting the offer, not a legal payment deadline.

warnings: This is not an official invoice or a Grundbuch (official land registry) matter: the sender is a private company offering a paid entry in its own unofficial, private register, and the small print explicitly says the entry has nothing to do with the official land register ('steht in keinem Zusammenhang mit dem amtlichen Grundbuch'). This matches a well-known German scam/aggressive-marketing pattern (similar to fake 'Gewerbeauskunft-Zentrale' letters) that relies on the invoice-like layout to make recipients believe payment is legally required.

The document itself states it is merely an offer and that no contract exists unless and until payment is made ('Dieses Schreiben ist ein Angebot... ein Vertrag kommt erst durch die Zahlung zustande') — so there is currently no payment obligation at all; paying would create one. Recommend not paying and, if desired, reporting the letter.

The printed IBAN (DE59 5007 0010 0005 5707 00) is formally valid and belongs to a German bank, but a valid IBAN does not confirm who the money actually goes to or that any registration will occur; do not use it without independently verifying the sender.
